1. (S) SITUATION:
Reinforcement shipping and fuel carriers are approaching Darwin while Soviet forces make a final eastern thrust against the coalition position in northern Australia. The convoy route is exposed in the Timor Sea and will be predictable to hostile reconnaissance and submarine patrols.
2. (S) MISSION: 2.1 Defend the Darwin convoy. 2.2 Destroy the enemy main thrust group. 2.3 {TaskForceFlagshipName} must survive.
3. (S) EXECUTION: 3.1 Establish a layered screen around the reinforcement convoy and remain between the shipping and the enemy approach axis. 3.2 Detect and engage the main thrust group before it can reach the convoy safe area. 3.3 Keep your Task Force reconnaissance aircraft on the main approach axis and coordinate with surface surveillance, giving priority to contacts that threaten the fuel carriers. 3.4 Escort the convoy into the marked Darwin exit corridor and retain the flagship until the convoy is safe.
4. (S) ENEMY SITUATION: 4.1 A Soviet surface force is expected to lead the final eastern thrust. 4.2 Long-range air reconnaissance and submarine interference are likely along the convoy route. 4.3 The enemy may attempt to bypass the escort and attack the slower fuel carriers directly.
5. (S) FRIENDLY SITUATION: 5.1 {TaskForceName} is the principal convoy defense and surface combat force. 5.2 Coalition reinforcement shipping and fuel carriers are the protected force. 5.3 Darwin provides the destination, air support, and recovery area once the convoy enters protected waters.
6. (S) INTEL ASSESSMENT: 6.1 Dry-season visibility favors detection but also gives hostile reconnaissance a clear view of the convoy route. 6.2 Enemy commanders are expected to accept losses if they can break the convoy screen before reaching Darwin. 6.3 Convoy survival is the primary measure of success. Do not pursue a damaged raider outside the screen if doing so exposes the shipping.
